_about: Per-tab CCL manifests (voice_guide_redesign.md sections 3, 8, 9). Each tab declares its supported verbs (caps) and its knob dimensions with a DOM binding + spoken aliases. Consumed by BOTH the shell (explorer.html builds the active tab's ctx from this) and the coverage audit (every live interactive control on a tab must be a bound knob or an explicit exclusion -- unbound control => loud pre-push failure, section 9). Adding a T1 tab is ONE entry here plus a knowledge default file -- never a new tool, prompt, or session-schema change. Knob `values[].v` are the real DOM option values (NOT their display labels); `aka` are the spoken forms a user would say. A knob carries `aka` too, because the word PRINTED on a control is not always its id -- metabolism's `metric` select is labelled Amplitude on screen, so `label` must mirror the live UI text and `aka` must cover what a user would actually say. Knob names and aliases MUST be single tokens: the parser takes `set <knob> <value...>` and reads the knob as the first word, so a two-word alias is unparseable, not merely unmatched. Keys beginning with _ are documentation and ignored by consumers. GESTURES: each tab must also declare its non-DOM interaction surface (zoom, pan, drag, click, hover) -- the runtime sweep enumerates ELEMENTS and is structurally blind to gestures, so they are declared and the gate checks the declaration is honest: `covered` must name verbs the tab actually has in caps, `deferred` must name its increment, `excluded` must give a reason, and a tab declaring nothing FAILS (silence is not a completeness claim).

sociogram._knobs_note: Sociogram's affordances are filters/selection/highlight/camera (their own dim kinds, not `set` knobs). It carries no `set` verb in v1. Listed here so the shell can read one uniform per-tab source; its caps mirror the engine's SOCIOGRAM_CAPS until step 2 migrates the shell to read caps from this file.

sociogram._coverage_note: Authored 2026-07-25 from the LIVE runtime sweep (window.CCLAudit), not from reading the HTML -- 84 interactive controls, of which the static file shows only a fraction (the 32 group checkboxes are innerHTML written at boot). THREE categories on purpose: dim_coverage = reachable today; controls_excluded = outside the voice surface with a reason; controls_deferred = IN scope and NOT yet reachable -- a real north-star gap, reported loudly by the audit and asserted exactly by scripts/test_voice_shell.cjs so new controls cannot quietly join the list. Deferred is not a synonym for excluded; collapsing the two is how this gate would rot.

agents_tab._caps_note: A three-view tab with no graph of its own to filter: what it CAN do is be moved between views, walked and read. `go schedule|sociogram|explorer` rides the existing sub-view declaration -- the same machinery Community Explorer uses, which is why this tab needed a manifest rather than new code (Tom, 2026-07-26: 'Agent Map has subtabs: should those be now navigable?'). They were not, because sub-views are DECLARED per tab and this tab was one of the nine still undeclared.
agents_tab._views_note: Three of these names -- sociogram, explorer, and the old aka `map` -- also name real TABS, which made them unreachable: destinations.json is authoritative and sub-views resolve only on `unresolved`, so `go sociogram` matched the Sociogram TOOL every time and threw the user across the app (Tom, 2026-07-26). Fixed in the shell, not by renaming: standing on a tab, that tab's own view wins, and `go <name> tab` forces the tab. `map` was still dropped as an alias because it collides with this tab's OWN name. The sociogram sub-view LAZILY fetches a ~25 MB artifact on first entry -- going there is a real download, not a toggle.

items._note: Rows are re-rendered on every filter/sort, so the roster is read live rather than cached. The table shows the FILTERED count and #exp-count carries 'N / M agents', so `what` can say which.

The schedule view draws its agents into a CANVAS, so the agents themselves are not DOM and cannot be walked until the canvas/data-bound adapter exists (prs_3d increment). What IS addressable is the legend: the categories, with counts. Declared honestly as categories rather than pretending the agents are reachable here.

The sociogram sub-view is a ~25 MB nested artifact with its own globals -- a graph roster there is the same work as the Community Explorer graph and prs_3d, not a reuse of the Sociogram's bespoke adapter.

curriculum_tools._caps_note: The first tab whose roster lives BEHIND the click. Parts and questions start closed, so `pick`/`next` -- which only ever MARKED an item -- could reach nothing here at all: with the tree collapsed there is nothing revealed to pick from, and no verb that opens it. So this tab is the one that made `open` general. `open` existed already but was wired to openNodeByLabel, a global that lives on wiki_narration.html and nowhere else, which is why every tab since the Sociogram has had to leave it out of caps. It is now DECLARED per item spec (`activate`), the same way `frame` and `total` are.

knobs.label: Show article rows
knobs._note: Not a display preference. With it OFF, clicking a QUESTION stops expanding and jumps straight to that question's first available article (onClickQuestion) -- so the identical spoken command would mean two different things depending on a checkbox the voice user cannot see. The items spec therefore declares `requires_knob` and the shell puts it ON before walking, out loud (Tom, 2026-07-27: bind it, force it on before pick).

knobs.label: Summa-in-1-year Transcript
knobs._note: A SETTING, not a place: it changes how the open article is rendered, not which article you are on -- so it is a knob rather than a sub-view. It is drawn as two buttons, which knobs could not bind (a <select> or a checkbox only), and its winning class is `.on`, not the `.active` a view's test hard-codes. Declaring it as a view would have been mis-declaring it to fit the machinery; the `buttons` bind kind is the honest fix and is portable to every button-group toggle in the fan-out. Both sides are gated on the entry actually HAVING that file (switchMode returns early otherwise), and neither does anything until an article is open.

curriculum_tools._views_note: `sociogram` names a real TAB as well, the third such collision in six manifests, and it is a TRUE sub-view rather than a name to rename away: it pulls in the Sociogram tool pre-cut to Summa nodes via applySummaSociogramPreset (Tom, 2026-07-27: 'just as under the Agent Map'). No new mechanism was needed -- 69c312d already settled this exact case: standing on a tab, that tab's own view wins, `go sociogram tab` forces the tool, and `go sociogram of curriculum tools` works from anywhere. Entering it LAZILY fetches wiki_narration.html, a ~28.7 MB artifact, on first entry: going there is a real download, not a toggle -- the same warning the Agent Map's sociogram view carries.

requires_knob.why: with it off, a question click jumps to an article instead of expanding, so `open` would have two meanings

items._note:
ONE FLAT ROSTER OF VISIBLE ROWS at all three levels, not three level-scoped rosters. `when` can only ask which sub-view is active, and nothing on this page says which LEVEL a user is walking -- there is no such state to read, because a sighted user is not at a level either, they are looking at an open tree. So `next` walks exactly the visual reading order and `open` on a part or a question expands it, which makes the roster GROW as you go. That growth is reported, because expanding a container and loading an article are the same verb on the same tree and would otherwise sound identical.
NO `total` DECLARED, deliberately. #stats-line counts ARTICLES (2656 of 2747 available) while this roster counts ROWS; wiring it up would make `what` say '24 of 2747 entries', which is false in unit rather than merely imprecise. Speaking the availability line honestly is its own declaration -- curriculum tools increment 2.
`.a-row.avail` only: 91 articles have no transcript yet and carry NO click handler at all, so offering them would be offering a door that does not open.
items._reads_note: Where the page PUTS what a row opens. Without it `read` spoke the tree row -- 'A1 Article 1 Day 2', five words -- and called it the article. The row is a door, not the room; only the page knows which pane it renders into.

items._note: The Summa sociogram is the wiki_narration graph one document down, pre-cut to Summa nodes. Its nodes are walkable in principle -- revealedNodes() already knows this exact artifact -- but that reader is hard-wired to the tab's OWN document (ifWin/ifDoc) and does not take a frame the way domItems does. Generalising it is the prs_3d increment's job, not this one's, so the view is reachable and honest about being unwalkable rather than silently returning an empty roster.
